definition: computer systems able to perform tasks that normally need human thinking
example: Advances in artificial intelligence are changing how doctors read medical scans.

definition: a set of step-by-step rules that a computer follows to solve a problem
example: The algorithm ranks search results according to hundreds of different signals.

definition: the use of machines to do work that people used to do
example: Automation has eliminated many routine office jobs while creating a demand for technical skills.

definition: the protection of computer systems and data from attack
example: Hospitals must invest in cybersecurity because a single attack can shut down life-saving equipment.

definition: an incident in which private information is accessed or stolen without permission
example: A data breach at the retailer exposed the credit card details of millions of customers.

definition: the process of turning information into a code so unauthorised people cannot read it
example: Strong encryption protects messages from being read by anyone except the intended recipient.

definition: software designed to damage a computer or steal information
example: Clicking on a suspicious link can silently install malware on your laptop.

definition: a fraudulent attempt to trick people into giving personal information by email or message
example: Phishing emails often imitate banks and urge recipients to confirm their passwords.

definition: a security system that blocks unauthorised access to a computer network
example: The company's firewall blocked thousands of suspicious connection attempts every day.

definition: the amount of data that can be sent over a connection in a given time
example: Rural schools with limited bandwidth struggle to run video lessons.

definition: a fast internet connection that carries a large amount of data
example: Many villages still lack reliable broadband, which limits opportunities for small businesses.

definition: using radio or similar signals instead of cables
example: Wireless networks have made it possible to work from cafes and parks.

definition: the ability of devices or places to connect to a network or to each other
example: Poor connectivity in remote regions prevents farmers from checking market prices online.

definition: the gap between people who have access to modern technology and those who do not
collocations: the digital divide between rich and poor
example: Free public computers in libraries can help narrow the digital divide.

definition: the ability to find, evaluate and use information through digital devices
example: Digital literacy is as important for older adults as for children, given how many services have moved online.

definition: a mobile phone that can run applications and connect to the internet
example: Most teenagers now spend several hours a day on a smartphone.

definition: a small device with a particular practical purpose
example: He buys every new gadget as soon as it comes onto the market.

definition: an electronic device worn on the body, such as a fitness band
example: A wearable that tracks heart rate can alert users to irregular rhythms.

definition: a computer-created environment that users can explore as if it were real
example: Surgeons can rehearse complex operations in virtual reality before working on real patients.

definition: technology that adds digital images or information to a view of the real world
paraphrases: digital overlay on the real world
example: Augmented reality lets museum visitors see a dinosaur appear in the room around them.

definition: the design, building and use of robots
example: Progress in robotics has made it possible for machines to assist elderly people at home.

definition: an aircraft without a pilot that is controlled remotely
example: Farmers now use a drone to inspect crops across large fields in a matter of minutes.

definition: a form of artificial intelligence in which computers improve by analysing data
example: Machine learning allows banks to spot unusual spending patterns that might signal fraud.

definition: extremely large collections of information that can be analysed to reveal patterns
example: Retailers use big data to predict what customers will buy before they search for it.

definition: the use of remote servers on the internet to store and process data
example: Cloud computing lets small firms use powerful software without buying expensive equipment.

definition: the programs that run on a computer
example: The latest software update fixed several security weaknesses in the system.

definition: the physical parts of a computer system
example: Outdated hardware slows down research because experiments take far longer to process.

definition: a computer system or website on which services or applications run
example: The company built a platform that links freelancers with clients around the world.

definition: the way in which a user interacts with a computer or application
example: An intuitive interface makes the application easy for older users to navigate.

definition: easy to understand and use
example: The banking app is so user-friendly that even my grandmother can transfer money with it.

definition: to replace something with a newer or better version
example: The university decided to upgrade its computer laboratories to meet student demand.

definition: no longer used because something newer and better has replaced it
example: Many typing skills have become obsolete since voice recognition improved.

definition: using the most modern methods and equipment available
example: The state-of-the-art laboratory attracted researchers from across the continent.

definition: introducing new ideas or methods
example: Innovative start-ups are developing cheaper ways to purify water.

definition: to completely change the way something is done
example: Mobile payment systems have revolutionised the way people shop in developing countries.

definition: the first model of a new product, used for testing before it is produced in quantity
example: Engineers tested the prototype for months before releasing the product to the public.

definition: an official right to be the only person to make or sell an invention
example: The firm filed a patent to stop competitors copying its new design.

definition: a new device or method created for the first time
collocations: the invention of the printing press
example: The invention of the printing press made books available to ordinary people.

definition: to make a process work by itself using machines or computers
example: Companies that automate routine tasks can free employees to focus on creative work.

definition: to convert information into a digital format
example: The library plans to digitise its oldest manuscripts so that scholars can consult them anywhere.

definition: the buying and selling of goods over the internet
example: The growth of e-commerce has forced many high-street shops to close.

definition: using electronic payment instead of notes and coins
example: Critics of a cashless society worry that elderly people will be unable to pay for basic goods.

definition: the right to keep personal information and activities secret
example: Many users accept long terms and conditions without realising how little privacy they are left with.

definition: laws and measures that keep personal information safe
example: Stronger data protection rules oblige firms to explain how they use customers' details.

definition: the amount of time spent looking at a phone, computer or television
paraphrases: hours in front of a screen
example: Experts recommend limiting screen time for young children before bed.

definition: depending too much on something
example: An over-reliance on calculators may weaken pupils' ability to do mental arithmetic.

definition: skilled and confident in using modern technology
example: My tech-savvy younger brother fixed the router in a few minutes.

definition: a very small piece of silicon that carries electronic circuits
example: Every modern car contains hundreds of microchips that control everything from brakes to windows.

definition: the part of a computer that carries out instructions
example: A faster processor lets the software analyse images in a fraction of a second.

definition: to copy a file from the internet onto your own device
example: I usually download podcasts before a long journey so I can listen offline.

definition: a website that finds information on the internet according to the words you type
example: A search engine can return millions of results in less than a second.

definition: a large organised collection of data stored on a computer
example: The police are creating a national database of fingerprints to speed up investigations.

definition: using physical features such as fingerprints to identify a person
example: Many phones now use biometric scanners instead of passwords.

definition: technology that identifies people by analysing the features of their faces
example: Some cities have banned facial recognition in public spaces because of privacy concerns.

definition: a digital record of transactions shared across many computers that is very hard to alter
example: A blockchain stores each transaction in a linked sequence that cannot easily be changed.

definition: a digital form of money that uses encryption and is not controlled by a bank
example: The value of a cryptocurrency can change dramatically within a few hours.

definition: the process of making solid objects by building them up layer by layer from a digital design
example: 3D printing allows hospitals to produce custom replacement parts for patients on site.

definition: the science and use of extremely small structures at the scale of atoms and molecules
example: Nanotechnology may eventually allow drugs to be delivered directly to cancer cells.

definition: the sending of information over distances by phone, radio or the internet
example: The telecommunications industry has invested billions in building faster mobile networks.

definition: an object sent into space to collect information or relay signals
example: Satellite images enable scientists to monitor changes in forests from far above.

definition: a house with devices that can be controlled automatically or by phone
example: In a smart home, lights and heating can be adjusted by voice command.

definition: a small fault that stops something working properly
example: A glitch in the booking system meant that several customers were charged twice.

definition: a failure to work in the correct way
example: A single malfunction in the control system forced the whole plant to shut down.

definition: a spare copy of data kept in case the original is lost
example: Always make a backup of your essay before you switch off the computer.

definition: a secret word or code that allows someone to enter a system
example: Using the same password for every account makes it easy for criminals to break in.

definition: the state of not being identified by name
example: Online anonymity can encourage honest discussion but also abusive behaviour.

definition: the trail of data that a person leaves when using the internet
example: Employers may examine a candidate's digital footprint before making a job offer.

definition: a video or recording created by software to make someone appear to say or do something they did not
example: A convincing deepfake of the president circulated for hours before it was exposed as fake.

definition: a computer program that talks with people in everyday language
example: Many banks now answer simple queries through a chatbot rather than a human adviser.

definition: changing an industry or way of doing things in a major, unexpected way
example: Ride-hailing apps proved to be a disruptive force for the traditional taxi industry.

definition: the process of becoming out of date and no longer used
example: Critics accuse manufacturers of planned obsolescence, designing phones that fail after a few years.

definition: the network of everyday objects that are connected to the internet and exchange data
collocations: devices in the internet of things
example: The internet of things allows a fridge to order food when supplies run low.

definition: a person who gains unauthorised access to computer systems
example: A hacker broke into the council's network and demanded payment to restore its files.

definition: existing or taking place on a computer rather than in the real world
example: Virtual meetings save companies the cost of flying employees across the globe.

definition: to be among the first to develop or use a new method or idea
example: The company pioneered a technique that allows complex parts to be produced in a single step.

definition: a compulsive need to use a mobile phone that harms daily life
example: Teachers report that smartphone addiction makes it harder for pupils to concentrate in class.
